subject: Sponsor decision checkpoints & security evidence plan
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Meera Singh <meera.singh@helioshealth.com>, Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Sponsor decision checkpoints & security evidence plan

Hi Meera / Aaron —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our sponsor-level discussion and proposed next steps so your procurement and security teams have a single source of truth. High-level takeaways: 

- Primary pain: inconsistent inference latency at scale across multi-region traffic, plus rising per-token costs for batch scoring of clinical notes.
- Business goals: 99th-percentile latency <= 150ms for 1k/sec sustained requests in US regions; reduce inference unit cost by ~30% for batch scoring within 90 days of rollout.
- Decision criteria (sponsor): predictable latency, auditable security posture (SOC 2 + deployment controls), and clear procurement path with price transparency.

Specific risk items we noted:
- Data residency requirement for PHI-derived data processing (must stay in us-west-2 or on-prem).
- Need for SOC 2-type evidence and TLS+KMS integration details before legal signs off.
- Contingency for latency spikes: automatic fallback to smaller model family with clear SLA tolerances.

Proposed next steps / owners:
1) I will share an initial "security & procurement checklist" (attached) with the asks we discussed — Alex (today EOD).
2) Meera: confirm procurement committee members and target contract approval date (you mentioned late June).
3) Redwood will produce a short SOC2 summary + deployment options doc that maps to your control sets — Karthik (by Thu 5/20).
4) Schedule 30-min follow-up with Helios security and operations to validate KMS/HSM integration (week of 5/24) — Laura to coordinate.

Attachments: Helios_Risk_Checklist_v1.xlsx (stub) — single-sheet checklist summarizing controls & evidence requests.

If I've missed anything, flag it and I will update. Otherwise I'll proceed with the SOC2 summary and set up the ops call.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Meera Singh <meera.singh@helioshealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sponsor decision checkpoints & security evidence plan

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and the checklist. Two quick clarifications from our side: 

- Decision timeline: procurement committee will review vendor materials week of Jun 21, target legal signature by Jun 30 (so your suggested late June works).
- Committee members: Aaron Cole (CISO), Priya Mehta (Sr. Dir, Legal), and myself (VP Product). Aaron will be the primary security reviewer.

Security asks to add to the checklist:
- Copy of recent SOC 2 Type II report (or SOC 2 readiness evidence),
- Documentation of network segmentation options for private deployments,
- Confirmation of ability to pin model versions and KV cache retention controls.

We can meet the week of 5/24 for a focused 30-min session — prefer Tue or Wed mornings PT. Laura, if you can propose 2 slots that works for Redwood, we will confirm.

Thanks — Meera
Meera Singh
VP, Product | Helios Health
meera.singh@helioshealth.com

Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sponsor decision checkpoints & security evidence plan

Appreciate the recap. Two security-specific follow-ups: 

1) SOC 2: we need a redacted SOC 2 Type II report or a vendor attestation + recent penetration test summary. If you cannot provide a full SOC 2 yet, a maturity report mapping your controls to our control IDs will suffice for the initial review.

2) Runtime isolation & PHI controls: can you provide a short note on the private deployment options (VPC vs on-prem) and what KMS/HSM integrations look like in each? Also describe whether Redwood supports per-tenant keying and KV cache TTL controls.

Pilot scope: Aaron
- We'd like a 4-week pilot limited to non-production PHI-reduced data to validate latency and cost curves. Will need clear rollback criteria (latency >200ms 99th or error rate >1%).

I can share our procurement packet template after you send the SOC2 summary; that will speed legal review.

Aaron Cole
CISO | Helios Health
aaron.cole@helioshealth.com
